Maya (CS): Quick thread — putting together a short customer-facing playbook for prefill/prefetch vs on-demand. want something we can hand to customers during onboarding.
Alejandro (Solutions): Love it. high level bullets + a tiny config snippet would help.
Sasha (Eng): Agree. include recommended batch window numbers + streaming toggle guidance depending on latency profile.
Maya (CS): Draft thoughts: 1) If customer has predictable prompts, use prefill (edge cache TTL 1–6h). 2) For interactive chat with short sessions, prefer client-side debounce + small server batching. 3) Streaming ON for long generative responses; OFF for tiny classification calls.
Jin (PM): Add renewal-risk signal: falling active convo count >40% over 14d = escalate. also missing onboarding callbacks in 7d -> outreach.
Alejandro (Solutions): Add example config block we can paste into onboarding guide:
```yaml
prefetch:
  enabled: true
  ttl_seconds: 3600 # 1h for friendly UX
client:
  debounce_ms: 150
server_batch:
  max_wait_ms: 50
  max_batch_tokens: 2048
streaming:
  enabled_for_long_responses: true
```
Sasha (Eng): Implementation notes for customers: - client debounce avoids duplicate user clicks - server batch window tradeoff: 30–80ms favors latency, 80–200ms favors throughput/cost. - KV cache keys: include tenant-id + prompt-hash.
Maya (CS): OK to give this as "recommended defaults" in the first 90-day onboarding doc?
Alejandro (Solutions): Yep. For enterprise, mention dedicated capacity and can tighten TTLs for PII-sensitive workloads.
Jin (PM): Also include a short checklist for enablement handoff: 1) Confirm sample prompt corpus 2) Set bounce-back plan (if cache miss spike) 3) Agree telemetry events + smoke test times.
Maya (CS): Draft outreach template to capture feedback post-onboarding: "Hey — quick 3 q's about model relevance, latency satisfaction, and any weird outputs. reply here or fill [short form]". keep it <60s.
Sasha (Eng): Add troubleshooting snippet for bursty drops: run this to check client queue/backpressure:
```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/tenants/{id}/metrics?window=5m | jq '.throughput, .latency_p95'
```
ops-bot: deploy/finished Maya's-playbook-v0.1 by alejandro at 2024-04-11T16:45:12Z :white_check_mark:
Maya (CS): Beautiful. I'll surface this in tomorrow enablement call and attach the snippet and the 3-question feedback template. anyone want to add an SLA note?
Alejandro (Solutions): Add a note: if customer uses hosted tier, call out per-token cost impact when TTL is long vs heavy live queries. one sentence.
Jin (PM): I'll add renewal-risk threshold language and link to the renewal playbook.
Maya (CS): Great — final ask: can Sasha give a 2-line dev note about streaming CPU overhead so customers understand cost tradeoffs?
Sasha (Eng): 2-liner: "Streaming keeps connections open and slightly increases per-request CPU; best for responses >300 tokens or interactive typing UX. For sub-100-token responses, prefer non-streaming to save cycles."
Maya (CS): Perfect. thanks team — will push the playbook into the onboarding folder and ping the enablement group. :sparkles:
